name: store
label: App Store
description: A package manager for apps, on top of git. Add a store (a folder or a git repository with app packages and an index.json), pull to fetch, install an app into modules, publish an installed app back to a store, and remove one. Each app shows its category, description, version, author and whether it is certified.

steps: Open Apps > App Store. Add a store with a name and either a git url (https://github.com/you/apps.git, pulled with git) or a blank url, which makes it a local folder under data\store\<name>. The catalogue is that folder's index.json plus one directory per app.

Pull fetches a git store (or rescans a local one). Install copies the app folder into modules\ and it appears in Apps without a restart - pages, a pane tab if the manifest asks for one, tools and routes. An app that is already installed offers reinstall; that replaces it, and it asks first.

Every card lists what the package can do, measured from its files rather than taken from its manifest: 'same-origin page' means the page runs inside this dashboard and can read what it can; 'server code' means a .psm1 runs in PowerAgent's own process with your files, credentials, network and ability to start processes; 'python' is a child process under the same user. The hash badge means the store publishes a digest for the package and it is checked before anything is copied; 'no hash' means nothing is verified. Pressing install explains all of it and asks you to confirm. docs\PAS_SECURITY.md is the long version.

Publish an installed app into a store: it copies source only (no .venv, __pycache__, node_modules, logs), bumps the manifest version first so one number never means two builds, merges the index.json entry, and commits and pushes when the store has a remote. Give the app a category and a description in its module.json first - the store listing reads them.
fixes: Install says the app already exists

That is the store refusing to overwrite silently: reinstall (it asks) replaces modules\<app> with the store copy, or remove the app first. Your local edits to that app are lost either way - publish them to a store if they matter.
Install fails with 'the package has no <name>.html page'

A page is only required when the app ships one. A page-less package is fine when it declares toolsFunction, routes, startFunction, avatars or a runtime - a Python app ("runtime": "python") serves its own page through /api/py/<name>/ even with "pane": true. A package with neither a page nor any of those is refused as junk. This was a bug that made about twenty store apps, including the two Python ones, uninstallable - update PowerAgent if it still happens.

A git store needs git on this machine and credentials for a private repo; a local store has no pull, only a rescan of its folder. A store that was never cloned is cloned on the first pull, so a wrong url shows up as a clone error, not an empty list.
The app is in the store but not in Apps after installing
Check Settings > Features: an app whose manifest has enabledByDefault false, or one you turned off, is installed but greyed out. Apps > Modules lists it either way.
Install refused: 'does not match the hash in the store's index.json'

The package folder no longer matches what was published - somebody edited it in the store clone, or a pull left it half-written. Nothing was copied. Re-pull the store, or re-publish the app from a trusted copy; a deliberate rehash is pwsh -File .\store-hash.ps1 (try -WhatIf first). force does not bypass this, by design.

That store publishes no sha256 for the app, so the folder was copied as it stood. It is not a failure, only an absence of proof: rehash the store with store-hash.ps1, or publish the app again, and the next install is verified.
